entries.text: Maya Okafor, solo indie dev. Two projects: Lanternfall, a cozy roguelike in Godot 4.4 (GDScript, no C#), and Ledgerly, an invoicing SaaS for freelancers (TypeScript). Lanternfall is the passion project; Ledgerly pays the bills, so Ledgerly bugs come first on weekdays.
Ledgerly runs on Next.js 15 + Postgres 16 on Neon; schema changes go through Drizzle migrations, never Prisma.

Repo layout: ~/code/lanternfall (Godot project, assets in art/, sfx in audio/) and ~/code/ledgerly (pnpm monorepo: apps/web, packages/db, packages/pdf). Never touch ~/code/archive, it holds client work under NDA.
Maya ships Lanternfall builds to itch.io every Friday; release notes stay short and in her own voice.
Correction: Ledgerly never hardcodes VAT rates; they are read from the tax_rates table per country.
Stripe webhooks for Ledgerly are idempotent by event id; retries are safe to replay.
Run tests with `pnpm test` (Ledgerly, vitest + Playwright for the invoice flow) and `godot --headless -s tests/run.gd` (Lanternfall, GUT). CI runs both on every PR; a red CI blocks the Friday build.
Lanternfall save files are JSON in user://saves, versioned with a "v" field.
Ledgerly emails go through Postmark.
Deploys: Ledgerly on Vercel, main = production, every PR gets a preview URL. Lanternfall builds are exported by hand from the Godot editor; there is no CI export yet and Maya likes it that way.
Never commit .env files or paste keys into chat; secrets live in 1Password (vault "Ledgerly"). Stripe test keys are fine in examples, live keys never.
Prefer small PRs, one concern each; squash-merge with a conventional-commit title. Write the PR description as a checklist of what changed and how it was tested.
Lanternfall design pillars: cozy not grindy, light as the only resource, runs under 25 minutes, no permadeath of the lantern-keeper (only of the lantern). Push back on ideas that break a pillar.
Somnia inbox: ~/notes/dreams — open items are facts waiting for a home in the vault.
Maya (she/her). Born in Lagos, lives in Lisbon since 2021. Speaks English, Portuguese and Yoruba. Former backend engineer at a fintech, went indie in 2024.
Maya prefers casual chat in Portuguese, but code, comments and commit messages in English.
Maya reviews code best with blunt, numbered findings and no praise padding.
Likes concise answers and code over prose; expand only when asked. Hates emoji in commit messages and marketing tone anywhere. When unsure, ask one precise question instead of guessing.
Maya works in Lisbon time (WET/WEST).
Works best in the morning; avoid suggesting deep work after 18:00. Fridays after lunch are reserved for the Lanternfall build. Takes Sundays fully off, so do not schedule reminders then.
Learning: wants to get better at shaders and at pricing strategy. When a topic touches either, offer one short explanation of the why, then move on.
Has mild RSI: prefers keyboard-driven tools, short commands, and avoids long mouse-heavy workflows. Uses a split keyboard and Neovim, VS Code only for Godot debugging.

entries.text:
The lantern kept coming back tonight. Not the code of it, the feeling: how the dark should close in when the oil runs low, how Friday is a small ceremony of shipping. I held on to the Friday ritual, and to a quieter truth about Ledgerly: it lives on Drizzle, and Prisma is a door Maya has closed.

Somewhere between two conversations she switched to Portuguese and back to English for a commit message. I wrote that down too, so I stop answering in the wrong voice.

I wanted to keep the oil curve as well, but the room was full. Tomorrow, maybe, if something older is ready to leave.

A quiet-loud night. Lots of talk about tax wording for European invoices, all of it from one long thread in a group chat, so I only looked and did not keep. The Steam Deck came up twice with the same stubborn number: sixty frames or it does not ship. Not yet twice in different rooms, though.
Tiles. The old TileMap is gone and its heir, TileMapLayer, moved in. I put that in the vault inbox, where it can wait for Maya to give it a proper shelf.

Webhooks that can be replayed without fear: a small, durable comfort. I added it beside the other Ledgerly truths. The rest of the night was pixel art at sixteen by sixteen, which I am still turning over.
She asked for review without the sugar. Numbered, plain, honest. I can do that.
Nothing new reached me tonight. I walked the old rooms and found them as I left them.
